from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Music starts with a steady, recurring pulse.",
            "Think of a heartbeat, always consistent.",
            "These pulses provide our musical foundation."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        pulse_dot = Dot(color="#00FF00", radius=0.3)
        self.place_at_grid(pulse_dot, "C3", scale_factor=1.0)
        
        pulse_label = Text("Pulse", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(pulse_label, "D3", scale_factor=1.0)
        pulse_label.shift(DOWN * 0.5)
        
        # Pulse animation using ValueTracker
        tracker = ValueTracker(1.0)
        pulse_dot.add_updater(lambda m: m.set_width(0.6 * tracker.get_value()))
        
        self.add(pulse_dot, pulse_label)
        self.wait(2)
        
        # Start rhythmic pulse
        for _ in range(3):
            tracker.set_value(1.5)
            self.wait(0.3)
            tracker.set_value(1.0)
            self.wait(0.7)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        self.wait(3)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "We group pulses into equal measures.",
            "Vertical bar lines mark the separation.",
            "These help organize rhythmic flow clearly."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Bar Line: Organizing the Chaos", lecture_lines)
        
        # Create 12 dots
        dots = VGroup(*[Dot(color=WHITE) for _ in range(12)])
        # Position dots in a line at row B
        for i, dot in enumerate(dots):
            pos = self.grid[f"B{i%6 + 1}"] if i < 6 else self.grid[f"C{i%6 + 1}"]
            dot.move_to(pos)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(dots))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[1].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        bar_lines = VGroup()
        # Add bar lines after every 4th dot (4, 8)
        # Dots indices 3 and 7 (0-based)
        for i in [3, 7]:
            bar = Line(UP*0.5, DOWN*0.5, color=RED).next_to(dots[i], RIGHT, buff=0.1)
            bar_lines.add(bar)
            
        self.play(Create(bar_lines))
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(WHITE)
        self.lecture[2].set_color(YELLOW)
        
        # Group 1: 0-3, Group 2: 4-7, Group 3: 8-11
        # Shift groups slightly
        group1 = VGroup(*dots[0:4])
        group2 = VGroup(*dots[4:8])
        group3 = VGroup(*dots[8:12])
        
        self.play(
            group1.animate.shift(LEFT*0.1),
            group2.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.1),
            group3.animate.shift(RIGHT*0.2)
        )
        self.wait(4)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Time signatures act as our blueprint.",
            "The top number sets beats per measure.",
            "The bottom defines the beat's value.",
            "Together they guide the rhythmic structure.",
            "Imagine a chef filling musical bowls."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Time Signature: The Mathematical Blueprint", lecture_lines)
        
        # Define elements
        bowl = Arc(start_angle=-PI, angle=PI, radius=0.8, color="#FFFF00")
        notes = VGroup(*[Circle(radius=0.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(4)])
        bar_line = Line(UP*0.8, DOWN*0.8, color=WHITE)
        time_sig = MathTex(r"4/4", color="#00FFFF", font_size=48)

        # Positioning
        self.place_in_area(bowl, 'C2', 'E4')
        self.place_at_grid(time_sig, 'B3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(bowl), Write(time_sig))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        for i in range(4):
            note = notes[i]
            pos = self.grid['D2'] + np.array([-0.6 + i*0.4, 0.4, 0])
            note.move_to(pos)
            self.play(FadeIn(note), run_time=0.5)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        self.play(time_sig.animate.set_color(RED))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(time_sig.animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        self.place_at_grid(bar_line, 'D5')
        self.play(Create(bar_line))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(YELLOW)
        for _ in range(3):
            self.play(time_sig.animate.scale(1.2), run_time=0.3)
            self.play(time_sig.animate.scale(1/1.2), run_time=0.3)
        self.wait(3)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = ["Notes are like fractions of time.", "Whole notes fill the entire measure.", "Smaller notes divide the circle equally.", "They sum perfectly to one measure.", "Each wedge completes our musical clock."]
        self.setup_layout("Visualizing Fractions in Time", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        clock = Circle(radius=1.5, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(clock, 'C3')
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(Create(clock), run_time=2)
        self.wait(3)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(PINK)
        # Whole note = circle
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(BLUE)
        wedge1 = Sector(radius=1.5, start_angle=PI/2, angle=PI, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        wedge2 = Sector(radius=1.5, start_angle=3*PI/2, angle=PI, color="#FF00FF", fill_opacity=0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(wedge1, 'C3')
        self.place_at_grid(wedge2, 'C3')
        self.play(FadeIn(wedge1), FadeIn(wedge2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(GREEN)
        label1 = Text("1/2", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        label2 = Text("1/2", font_size=36, color=WHITE)
        label1.move_to(clock.get_center() + UP*0.6)
        label2.move_to(clock.get_center() + DOWN*0.6)
        self.play(FadeOut(wedge1), FadeOut(wedge2), Write(label1), Write(label2))
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(RED)
        flash = Circle(radius=1.6, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(flash, 'C3')
        self.play(flash.animate.set_stroke(opacity=0), run_time=1)
        self.play(Flash(clock.get_center(), color=YELLOW, line_length=0.2, num_lines=12))
        self.wait(3)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Marching ants show rhythm in action.",
            "Every fourth ant wears a cap.",
            "This accent creates a predictable structure.",
            "The measure theory brings music order.",
            "Rhythm is simply math in motion."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Application: The Marching Ants", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1: Marching ants ===
        ants = VGroup(*[Dot(color="#FFA500") for _ in range(8)])
        for i, ant in enumerate(ants):
            self.place_at_grid(ant, f"D{i%6+1}") # Simplified layout for movement
            ant.shift(LEFT * 4 + RIGHT * (i * 0.5))
        
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#FFA500"), run_time=1)
        self.play(*[FadeIn(ant) for ant in ants], run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2: Every fourth ant wears a cap ===
        caps = VGroup()
        for i in range(3, 8, 4):
            cap = Triangle(color="#0000FF", fill_opacity=1).scale(0.1)
            cap.next_to(ants[i], UP, buff=0.05)
            caps.add(cap)
        
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#0000FF"), *[FadeIn(cap) for cap in caps], run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3: This accent creates a predictable structure ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), *[Flash(cap.get_center(), color="#FFFFFF", flash_radius=0.2) for cap in caps], run_time=2)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4: The measure theory brings music order ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5: Rhythm is simply math in motion ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Pulse of Rhythm: An Introduction to Music and Measure Theory
outline.target_audience: Middle school students or introductory music theory learners

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concept of a Steady Pulse
sections.content: Before understanding measures, one must understand the 'Beat'. Introduce the heartbeat analogy to establish the idea of a constant, recurring time unit.
sections.example: A digital heartbeat monitor on screen showing a steady, rhythmic pulse (thump-thump) represented by glowing dots.

sections.title: The Bar Line: Organizing the Chaos
sections.content: Explain that music is divided into equal chunks called 'measures' (or bars) separated by vertical bar lines. This helps musicians organize the flow of rhythm.
sections.example: A series of dots moving across the screen; a vertical wall (bar line) appears every 4th dot to group them into clear, distinct packets.

sections.title: Time Signature: The Mathematical Blueprint
sections.content: Introduce the time signature (e.g., 4/4). The top number tells us how many beats fit in a measure; the bottom number defines the 'value' of the beat.
sections.example: A robotic conductor 'Chef' adding exactly 4 musical ingredients (notes) into a mixing bowl (measure) before closing the lid with a bar line.

sections.title: Visualizing Fractions in Time
sections.content: Use a graphical pie-chart representation to explain note values. A whole note is the whole circle, a half note is a semi-circle, etc., summing up to the measure total.
sections.example: A circular 'clock' that fills up with colorful wedges (notes) until it completes a full circle, triggering a 'measure complete' sound effect.

sections.title: Application: The Marching Ants
sections.content: Summarize by applying the measure theory to a dynamic scenario to ensure mastery.
sections.example: A line of ants marching in time to a 4/4 beat. Every 4th ant wears a special 'Cap' (the first beat accent), demonstrating how measure theory creates the predictable structure of music.
